answer: Each bonded identity commits collateral, and evidence linking coordinated equivocation triggers a penalty that grows as O(k²) for k identities, rather than treating each fault in isolation. A detected sybil swarm therefore faces an exponential multiplier in total capital loss as coordination and exposure compound, making identity splitting uneconomic. A lagoon of aliases offers no shelter when a beacon links their votes; even a raven-like observer can verify the shared evidence.
